subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted boundary should OpenClaw enforce for model-visible SKILL.md content?
rationale: The fix defines a public security contract across prompt precedence, skills metadata, memory influence, tool authority, sandbox/profile behavior, and upgrade compatibility, so automation should not choose that boundary alone.

options.title: Design the boundary first
options.body: Define the skill precedence and capability contract, then implement enforcement and regression tests against that approved design.

options.title: Land scanner-only mitigation
options.body: Treat markdown scanning work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43469 as a partial hardening step while keeping this broader isolation issue open.

options.title: Defer runtime enforcement
options.body: Keep existing visibility and workshop scanning controls for now and revisit role/tool/memory enforcement as a larger security-profile program.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary first
recommendation.body: Define the skill precedence and capability contract, then implement enforcement and regression tests against that approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided maintainer-side security-review context on this issue and current source blame routes the central prompt/skills files through his recent commits.
